verified.exploit: borrowCrossChain snapshots source-chain collateral into the LZ payload but never locks it or records a pending borrow, and getHypotheticalAccountLiquidityCollateral counts nothing until the ValidBorrowRequest round-trip returns, so during the in-flight window the same collateral backs multiple cross-chain borrows (or is redeemed on the source chain) -> cross-chain debt unbacked by locked collateral.
verified.poc_sketch: Foundry two-endpoint LZ-mock: attacker supplies collateral C on chain A; issues borrowCrossChain(x,_borrowToken,B) and, before delivering the return ValidBorrowRequest, either (i) issues a second borrowCrossChain(x,_borrowToken,C_eid) — assert both dest chains authorise borrows summing to > C's collateral value — or (ii) calls CoreRouter.redeem of the full collateral on chain A (passes because userBorrowedAssets has no pending cross-chain borrow) then delivers the dest borrow; assert the dest chain hands out underlying while the source collateral no longer backs it.
verified.reason: borrowCrossChain neither locks collateral nor records a pending borrow on the source chain and does no source-side liquidity check (the debt is written only in _handleValidBorrowRequest after the full LZ round-trip), so the same stale collateral snapshot is sent to each destination and, since each destination validates payload.collateral only against its own local debt, an unprivileged attacker can fire concurrent in-flight borrows to different destination chains (or redeem on the source during the window) to have one collateral back debt exceeding it.
